messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: prod: high 5xx rate detected from frontdoor (ingress-gw). service=/api/generate, error_type=502/504 spike, P50 latency up. Paging: @jordan :rotating_light:

jordan: acked. I'm on it. linking dashboards and traces now.

maya: I can join — just finishing a deploy but can help with routing toggles.

ashok: noticed a simultaneous spike in retries from edge proxy to model backend around 11:42. Could be retry amplification + route weight change.

lance: customer-facing alert automation just flagged degraded API success rate > 5% for last 3m.

jordan: quick impact check — which customers/regions? I see most traffic hitting us from eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Not global outage but many production requests failing.

maya: logs: lots of 502s with upstream reset, and some 504s at gateway. Snapshot from edge logs: ```2026-02-17T11:42:12Z edge-proxy request_id=abc upstream_reset reason=connection_failure host=model-pool-1:443```

ashok: config-green rollout went out ~11:40 with a route weight tweak for canary. Could be we pushed a variant that trips circuit break thresholds.

jordan: timeline matches. Can we temporarily reduce retries at frontdoor and remove the new route weight change?

lance: recommend toggling `retry_policy` to minimal to avoid amplification. If Envoy applies retries to 5xx, that multiplies load.

jordan: steps I'm running now:
1) set frontdoor retry to 0 for /api/generate
2) pin route to stable pool (weight=100 stable, 0 canary)
3) scale up model-backend pods by +20%

maya: I'll prepare the config change. deploy-bot, can you apply a config rollback for route weights to stable?

deploy-bot: Received request to rollback route weight on ingress-config-prod. Running dry-run..

deploy-bot: Dry-run ok. Applying change now.

jordan: Running curl check against frontdoor after retry change: ````bash
curl -sv -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 'https://frontdoor.prod.redwood.ai/api/generate' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
````

jordan: initial check: 10/10 responses still 502. Backends still rejecting connections. Checking upstream pool health and circuit breaker stats.

maya: pulling Envoy admin stats: `cluster.model-backend-1.upstream_rq_pending_overflow` has spikes, `upstream_cx_overflow` present. That suggests connection pool limits.

ashok: interesting — we increased max connections in the backend earlier this week but maybe the canary variant has a different resource config and saturates.

lance: should we temporarily increase connection pool and circuit breaker thresholds? That risks masking root cause but might buy time.

jordan: prefer to reduce pressure first: remove retry amplification + re-route traffic to stable pool. If that doesn't relieve, we'll increase pool sizes.

maya: route rollback completed at 11:48 (deploy-bot confirmed). Frontdoor retry set to 0 at 11:49.

deploy-bot: Route weight change applied. Frontdoor retry policy updated.

jordan: re-running curl loop (every 5s) from us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Results: success slowly improving — 60% 200, 40% 502. Latency still elevated.

ashok: checking model-backend logs: a subset of instances are logging `fatal: handshake timeout` and then `connection reset` — likely overloaded. Those are exactly hosts the canary pointed to earlier.

jordan: action: isolate bad hosts from LB pool. maya, can you mark those hosts out in the service discovery / health check? I'll update weights to 0 for the failing nodes.

maya: marking nodes out now. Using `sdctl mark-out --service model-backend --host host-23,host-24,host-25` 11:52.

lance: after host removal I see immediate drop in upstream resets. Error rate trending down to ~3% within 2m.

jordan: good. Next: scale model-backend by +30% and monitor. Also file ticket to revert canary config and audit canary resource limits.

maya: scaling now via autoscaler override: `kubectl scale deployment/model-backend --replicas=39` — changed at 11:55.

deploy-bot: Autoscaler override accepted, scaling initiated.

jordan: monitoring: last 5m success rate now ~98% for /api/generate. Latency back to baseline. Confirming no big customer impact windows >5m.

lance: customer alert cleared. Notifying on support side to close incident-facing banner.

ashok: will collect config diffs: `git log --oneline` shows canary route change committed 11:39 and applied 11:40. Need a postmortem on the canary gating.

jordan: oncall handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. @kelly will take residual monitoring. Kelly, I'm leaving runbook pointers: playbook/link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/ingress-retry-cb

kelly: ack. I'll watch for regression and own follow-ups.

jordan: incident summary for ticket creation:
- root: canary route change applied that sent traffic to lower-capacity variant, which hit connection limits; frontdoor retries amplified the issue causing 5xx spike.
- mitigation: rolled back route weights, disabled retries, removed failing hosts from pool, scaled backend.
- impact: ~6 minutes elevated 5xx, ~majority customers unaffected but some production tenants saw errors.
- next steps: revert canary, add canary resource verification, add automation to detect retry amplification, and add circuit-breaker fallback to fail open slower.

maya: I'll own the follow-up to ensure canary config has required health gating and resource tags.

ashok: I'll draft incident ticket and RCA. tagging: #postmortem-team.

jordan: thanks all. closing thread and adding timestamped notes to incident ticket. If error rate climbs again, escalate to oncall-sre. :white_check_mark:
